front.title: Textual Representation of Autonomous System (AS) Numbers

abstract.t: A textual representation for Autonomous System (AS) numbers is defined as the decimal value of the AS number. This textual representation is to be used by all documents, systems, and user interfaces referring to AS numbers.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: A textual representation for Autonomous System (AS) numbers is defined as the decimal value of the AS number. This textual representation is to be used by all documents, systems, and user interfaces referring to AS numbers.

This document notes a number of potential representation formats and proposes the adoption of a decimal value notation for AS numbers, or "asplain" according to the representation taxonomy described here.

section.name: Taxonomy of Representation Formats
section.t: A taxonomy of representation for AS numbers is as follows:

dl.dd: refers to a syntax scheme of representing all AS numbers using decimal integer notation. Using asplain notation, an AS number of value 65526 would be represented as the string "65526" and an AS number of value 65546 would be represented as the string "65546".

refers to a syntax scheme of representing all AS numbers using a notation of two integer values joined by a period character: <high order 16-bit value in decimal>.<low order 16-bit value in decimal>. Using asdot+ notation, an AS number of value 65526 would be represented as the string "0.65526" and an AS number of value 65546 would be represented as the string "1.10".

refers to a syntax scheme of representing AS number values less than 65536 using asplain notation and representing AS number values equal to or greater than 65536 using asdot+ notation. Using asdot notation, an AS number of value 65526 would be represented as the string "65526" and an AS number of value 65546 would be represented as the string "1.10".

section.name: Representation of AS Number Values
section.t: To avoid confusion, a single textual notation is useful for documentation, configuration systems, reports, and external tools and information repositories. The decimal value representation, or "asplain" is proposed as the textual notation to use for AS numbers.

The "asplain" representation represents the number as its decimal value, without any field delimiter, corresponding to the lack of any internal structure required by the use of AS numbers in the inter-domain routing context.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA Registries should use decimal representation ("asplain") for AS numbers.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This document does not refer to matters associated with security of routing systems.

section.name: Acknowledgments
section.t: The terminology of "asplain", "asdot", and "asdot+" was originally devised and described by Juergen Kammer in January 2007 .
